column1: # The pages that a search of Nov 25, 2026 read for a rule on importing a graphics processor, an AI accelerator or a server: China's customs and tariff announcements of January 2024 to November 2026 with their annexes and explanations, and what was read beside them: 131 saved pages, one row each. 114 were read whole when the search ran; the last 17 rows are pages of the same search that could be saved only afterwards, by other routes (another address, another site's copy, a file host, an Internet Archive capture), and were read then, the three listing prospectuses among them in their passages on tariffs. Columns: the saved id; the rows of the search's list that rest on the page; its address and host; whether the host is a government's (told from the address; a reprint on another site of an official text counts as no); the page's title as saved; its length; the words that name Nvidia or one of its chips, and their count; the customs numbers under headings 8471, 8473 and 8542; and counts of thirteen words (chips, cards, servers; licence, inspection, check, hold, refusal to release; added duty; origin), each counted on the page as a visitor sees it, each text once: for a page saved from the web, the text the saved page shows, its menus, footers and side lists included, without its head, title, scripts and styles and without elements set not to display; for a PDF, its text layer; for the one Word file, the text extracted from it; the saver's own text file is not counted. Lengths and word counts are taken after all spaces are removed; the words naming Nvidia or one of its chips are 英伟达, 英偉達, 輝達, Nvidia in any case, H20, H200, H100, H800 and RTX; the customs numbers and the titles are given whole. 97 pages are on government hosts (86 of mainland bodies, 8 of Hong Kong's Trade and Industry Department, 3 of the United States: 2 of the White House and 1 of the Federal Register). A word naming Nvidia or one of its chips stands on 1 of the 97 (a white paper of the commerce ministry) and on 8 of the other 34 pages (company filings, a listing prospectus, brokers' reports, an industry association's notice, press); a customs number under 8471, 8473 or 8542 stands on 15 of the 97. One further page, a trade site's list of customs pre-rulings, prints the part number 6042B0934301, which another page of the table gives as NVIDIA's; that page names no maker, and the number is not counted as a word naming Nvidia. What the table cannot show: a measure that is not published. Not a census of every numbered customs announcement.
